summary.intent: Implement issue #2040: move the tick-loop closure body out of facade.rs into a new sync/pass.rs module, and move the scope-exit cut into rotation/, as part of an ongoing sync-pass refactor series, then push through review gates and land it.
summary.outcome: PR #2045 was merged after five commits, passing self-review gates (fmt/clippy/tests/wasm32/tracker-ref), a standards review, a spec review, a four-angle simplify pass, a security review, and CodeRabbit; issue #2037 was closed, follow-up issue #2056 filed, and work moved on to two parallel follow-ups (#2056 and #2041) which were interrupted by an Opus rate limit and relaunched.

repo: The tick closure in facade.rs is deeply entangled: moving it required widening visibility on SyncStatus fields, SweepKeys.scope_keys/owner_identity, SecondEnd, GraftedWritePass, SeedFloors, ConsultWindow, and the private child modules claim_conversion.rs/link_sweep.rs (pub(super) -> pub(crate))

Boundaries, ascent_node_seed, and proved_scope_ref were relocated from facade.rs to rotation/scope_material.rs (with rotation/mod.rs re-exporting pub(crate)) specifically so rotation/ no longer depends back on facade.rs for the scope-exit cut

TickPass::run in sync/pass.rs is the ordered list of 16 private stage methods that replaced the original tick closure; stage order and every await/RefCell borrow/event send point must remain identical to the original closure for it to be a strict refactor
facade.rs shrank from ~21998 to ~20592 lines (then sync/pass.rs itself was further trimmed from 1675 to 1385 lines) after the simplify pass removed per-stage field-list boilerplate
CONTEXT.md 'Sync and refresh' section is the canonical glossary location for new sync-related terms like 'Sync pass'
Comments that reference 'above'/'below' break when code is split into new functions during a move — must be re-anchored to name the specific stage instead of relying on physical proximity
EngineSeams<T,H,C,F,S,St,Sch> (sync/drain.rs:1142) and SessionState/SessionSecrets (session.rs:273/548) are the core structs threaded through every tick stage as pub(crate) Rc-wrapped fields
tracker-ref lint exempts '// #38 D4'-style frozen corpus citations from the orphaned-comment rule

code.finding: owner_identity (EcdsaVerifier, a Copy secp256k1 key) was initially copied by value (`let owner_identity = self.owner_identity;`) in three stages instead of borrowed; fixed to `&self.owner_identity` to match the original closure's single-borrow pattern

drain() originally needed #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)] with 8 args; refactored so Assembly holds descendants and ScopeSets holds proved/unproved scope sets, dropping drain to 6 args and removing the allow

Two #[cfg(test)] use imports (floor_namespace, expire_focus_stamps) were added at module level solely to keep unedited facade tests compiling after the move; identified as a follow-up to relocate into mod tests directly

workflow: When a background Explore/inventory agent surveys a file that another agent is concurrently editing, it can capture stale line numbers mid-edit — the agent itself flagged this and advised re-checking line numbers before applying its findings

Delegating a large mechanical move (identifiers + visibility inventory) to one Opus agent that also applies review fixes as follow-up commits keeps context/ownership with the agent that best understands the diff, rather than re-deriving context each round
Running standards review, spec review, and workspace clippy/wasm32 checks concurrently as independent background jobs (since none depend on each other) parallelizes the review-gate phase effectively

Batching multiple reviewer findings (standards + spec, or all 4 simplify angles) into one fix commit via SendMessage back to the implementing agent avoids fragmenting the branch history with many tiny commits
CodeRabbit reviews are rate-limited per PR/timeslot (~1 hour cadence observed: 23:00Z then next slot 00:34Z, then 01:09Z->02:09Z); must check elapsed time before requesting a new review
GitHub GraphQL secondary rate limits can be hit by long-running CI-watch polling loops; falling back to REST for status checks and comment posting works around it
Opus session limits can kill mid-flight worktree agents with no partial commits lost if they hadn't committed yet; relaunching with the same brief is safe in that case

friction: Facade.rs being edited concurrently by another process/agent caused the identifier-inventory Explore agent to report stale line numbers, requiring a re-check before applying its findings

GitHub GraphQL secondary rate limit was hit twice: once during CI-watch polling (had to TaskStop and fall back to REST) and once during the ready-flip/comment-post step (required a background retry loop)

Both parallel worktree agents (#2056 and #2041) were killed simultaneously by an Opus session rate limit (reset 4:50am Europe/Berlin), losing progress on two follow-up implementations though no commits were lost
Large diff output for the security-review skill was too large to inline (172.3KB) and had to be persisted to a scratch file
